# Office cases for the VBA project remover (unanswered)

Files are in this directory, written by the remover from the LibreOffice-written inputs (`lo-roundtrip.*`) or generated by `tools/VbaProbe remove <in> <out>`. Regenerate the outputs, hash them, and open each in the desktop application on the Office oracle machine; record the version and the outcome (opened, repair prompt text, anything missing).

| # | Input | Output | Ask |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lo-roundtrip.docm` | `.docx` | Word opens without a repair prompt; no macro warning bar; the document text is `Hello`. |
| 2 | `lo-roundtrip.xlsm` | `.xlsx` | Excel opens without a repair prompt; A1 is 1; the VBA editor shows no project. |
| 3 | `lo-roundtrip.pptm` | `.pptx` | PowerPoint opens without a repair prompt; one slide. |
| 4 | `lo-roundtrip.xls` | `.xls` | Excel opens without a repair prompt (record positions were corrected after dropping `ObProj`); no VBA project; A1 is 1. |
| 5 | a `.doc` with a `Macros` storage (any Word-saved macro document from the corpus) | `.doc` | Word opens without a repair prompt; no macros listed. |
| 6 | a `.ppt` with a VBA project (any PowerPoint-saved macro presentation) | `.ppt` | PowerPoint opens without a repair prompt; no macros; the emptied project record and the cleared `fHasMacros` do not trigger a repair. |
| 7 | each of 1–3 | Office's own "Save As" macro-free (`.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`) | The same parts removed as ours: list the part names of both packages and the main content type. |
| 8 | a macro-enabled file with a digitally signed project | ours and Office's de-macroed copy | Both open without a prompt; the signature part is gone in both. |
| 9 | a project with a password (Tools > VBAProject Properties > Protection) | `VbaProbe list` | Our locked flag is true and `HasPassword` true; Office shows the lock. |
| 10 | a project whose source was edited in a hex editor while the p-code was left (stomped) | `VbaProbe list` | Office shows the edited source or runs the p-code; record which, and whether `SourceAndPCodeMayDisagree` should be true. |

## Office run (Word, Excel and PowerPoint 16.0.20527)

Answered as far as the oracle can drive the applications: see the row for this request in [`docs/office-oracle-1.0.md`](../../docs/office-oracle-1.0.md#the-other-requests). Questions not listed there as run are still open.
